text:
sam_galbraith: Quick summary — during the 03/18 03:30 UTC incident we saw a sustained p95 latency spike on hosted-inference (routes: /v1/generate). Impact: ~12% increase in p95 for ~22m, error budget burn ~6% for the day. Root cause appears related to KV cache expiry churn + a rollout that increased seq length for a small subset of models. Postmortem is here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4521

maria_cheng: Noted. I'm starting an action tracker card list. We should split infra vs model/serving work. Recurring pattern: last 3 incidents show cache-miss storms when warmup traffic is low.

igor_petrov: I’ll own the KV cache investigation and remediation. Plan: 1) repro locally with load harness, 2) add TTL sanity checks and telemetry, 3) small canary fix. ETA: Thu EOD. @maria_cheng I'll add the ticket and link perf traces.

jess_t: I can update dashboards and alerts. Proposed changes: - add p50/p95/p99 per-route panels - add a rolling 30m error-budget-burn rule - alert if cache miss rate > 2% and p95 > 200ms. Grafana query I'd add for miss rate: `sum(rate(kv_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_request_total[5m]))`

product_ryan: From product POV we need to agree SLO behavior. Current p95 target 200ms, throughput target 400 req/s per shard. Given model seq-length shift we either: A) keep SLO and add mitigations (caching + batching) or B) temporarily adjust internal SLO tolerance while we patch. Prefer A. If we adjust public SLA we must loop in sales/legal.

sam_galbraith: Agreed with @product_ryan — don't change customer-facing SLA yet. Operational steps to reduce risk: (a) tagging: route-level sequence_length histogram (b) conservative autoscale bump for dedicated pools during canary (c) fail-open to smaller model variant when latency > 400ms.

maria_cheng: Action items I put into the tracker (INC-4521 follow-ups): - Igor: KV TTL checks + fix (owner: @igor_petrov, due: 2026-03-26) - Jess: Dashboard + error-budget alert (owner: @jess_t, due: 2026-03-24) - Infra: Autoscale policy review & temporary bump (owner: @sam_galbraith, due: 2026-03-23) - Product: SLO review doc and rollback criteria (owner: @product_ryan, due: 2026-03-25) - Ops: Add runbook step to failover to model-small variant (owner: oncall, due: 2026-03-24)

igor_petrov: I've created a branch and a small unit test that reproduces TTL drift. Will open PR and tag reviewers. Also adding bench harness steps to simulate long-tail sequences.

jess_t: Dashboard PR raised: https://github.com/redwood/grafana-dash/pull/321. Includes new panels and the 30m error budget alert. Requesting a quick review from @maria_cheng and @sam_galbraith.

sre_oncall_bot: Created ticket INC-4521-FU with subtasks and linked alert runbook. Reminder: recurring-incident label added.

sam_galbraith: Two quick asks: 1) can each owner add a single-line status update to the tracker by EOD tomorrow? 2) schedule a 30m follow-up sync on Fri 09:00 UTC to verify mitigations and SLO burn projections. I'll run capacity sims before the sync.

product_ryan: I'll draft an internal SLO rationale doc and include rollback criteria if burn > 15% over 72h.

maria_cheng: Thanks everyone — we'll classify this as "recurring cache miss" pattern and add to the Quarterly SRE risk register. Closing the thread until owners post EOD updates. :white_check_mark:
